Principle
Do not copy a product. Reuse its logic, then add a visual signature that belongs to your context.

Quiet core.

03 · Decision instrument

Patterns specific to Adoption Lane

The method becomes visible in the controls themselves.

Core shift: this is not merely a clean SaaS application. It is a decision-learning instrument. Inputs must look authored, history must remain visible, uncertainty must remain legible, and stopping must be presented as a valid outcome.
Judgment, not calculation

The Business–AI–Organization triangle

Use six discrete authored states from 0–5. No slider, numeric field, or star-rating metaphor.

Provenance in the mark

Inherited values announce their origin

Source information should be visible beside the value—not hidden in a tooltip or audit page.

04 · Composition rules

A reusable grammar for coding agents

Start with the work model

Identify objects, states, decisions, and recurring actions before choosing cards or gradients.

Choose one dominant navigation model

Sidebar, top navigation, canvas, or step flow. Avoid combining all four without a real reason.

Use tokens as constraints

Define surface, text, border, accent, radius, spacing, density, elevation, and motion before composing pages.

Design the dense state first

Real apps contain long names, warnings, empty fields, and competing actions. Test those before the polished demo state.

Add one signature system

Typography, texture, illustration, motion, or color logic. One strong system beats five weak effects.

Make mobile a different composition

Do not merely shrink desktop. Replace sidebars, keep touch targets usable, and surface the next action.

Anti-patterns

What makes SaaS look generated

Too many floating cards. Gratuitous gradients. Every section in a rounded container. Fake metrics. Decorative charts. Weak hierarchy. Giant empty hero areas inside operational tools. Color used without semantic meaning.

Card soupPurple glowDashboard cosplayNo real states
05 · Agent handoff

Prompt fragment you can reuse

Design a mobile-first SaaS interface as a coherent system, not a collage of fashionable components. PRODUCT CHARACTER - Quiet operational core - High information density where it supports decisions - One controlled visual signature - Fast for expert users; understandable when projected or read aloud SYSTEM - Use semantic design tokens for surfaces, text, border, accent, radius, spacing, density, elevation, and motion - Use accessible open-code primitives - Use one dominant navigation model - Place recurring actions consistently - Prefer progressive disclosure over visible control clutter - Include real states: loading, empty, error, blocked, long content, and mobile DECISION-INSTRUMENT BEHAVIOR - Render consultant judgments as discrete authored choices, not sliders or calculated-looking fields - Show provenance inline with inherited values - Preserve superseded values beside current values; never silently overwrite - Keep the fixed nine-station route visible at desktop and mobile scales - Represent uncertainty with a range plus explicit low / expected / high labels - Give Proceed and No-Go decisions equal visual prominence - Treat organizational-lens reflection as a first-class input that reappears in outputs VISUAL DIRECTION - Do not clone Linear, Vercel, Stripe, or shadcn - Borrow structural logic only - Avoid card soup, generic purple gradients, decorative charts, and fake metrics - Add identity through exactly one primary signature system: typography, texture, illustration, motion, or color logic DELIVER 1. Information architecture 2. Token set 3. Component inventory 4. Desktop composition 5. Mobile composition 6. Interaction states 7. Rationale for every non-standard visual choice
Research basis: Linear’s 2026 interface refresh and AI-age design writing; shadcn/ui’s open-code component model and Tailwind v4 support; current accessibility guidance; and 2026 graphic-design reporting on the move away from synthetic uniformity.
